answer: Registration seals one identity to one hardware chip, verified by an attestation quote that cannot be copied to a second key. A farm of 500 aliases needs 500 physical chips, each costing more than the epoch reward, so the attack is unprofitable before the first answer is even written. What carries the onyx here is verification, the wharf of cost is what stops the farm, and the willow of the record keeps every claim checkable.
